metrics_descriptions.Cost: Breakdown of residency status (In-State, Out-of-State, WUE), tuition tier, and expected financial aid impact.
metrics_descriptions.Difficulty: Selectivity and admission criteria (acceptance rate, GPA profile, and institutional rigor).
metrics_descriptions.Support: Availability and quality of academic advising, tutoring centers, freshman retention networks, and student success resources.
metrics_descriptions.Adjustment: Cultural transition and similarity to Southern California (lifestyle shift, regional dynamics, student body demographic balance).
metrics_descriptions.Home: Travel logistics back to San Diego (direct flight availability, drive times, airport proximity, and travel costs).
metrics_descriptions.Social: Weekend party environment, Greek life prevalence, off-campus house/bar scenes, and overall nightlife density.
metrics_descriptions.Environment: Proximity to outdoor recreation (beaches, trails, ski resorts, rivers) and access to active student lifestyle amenities.
metrics_descriptions.Weather: Count of pleasant/comfortable outdoor days during the core academic school year (Sept–May), excluding extreme heat, snow, or heavy rain.
metrics_descriptions.Biology: Institutional research funding (NIH/NSF), lab access, pre-health tracks, and proximity to biotech corridors.
metrics_descriptions.CLS: Alignment of biology curriculum with California Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) prerequisites (e.g., Hematology, Quant Chem) and clinical rotation pipelines.
metrics_descriptions.Spirit: Game day culture, D1 sports tradition, stadium energy, and collective student body pride.
metrics_descriptions.Happiness: Student quality-of-life rating based on campus safety, housing, food, community feel, and day-to-day satisfaction (anchored to Princeton Review QoL surveys).
metrics_descriptions.Admissions: Admissions: Selectivity, acceptance rates, test score profiles, and overall competitiveness of the admissions process.

profile.topology: Flat, coastal campus built on a bluff directly adjacent to the Pacific Ocean; exceptionally bike-friendly with extensive dedicated paths and flat terrain. Outdoors: Steps from the Pacific Ocean for immediate surfing, paddleboarding, and beach volleyball; 20 minutes to Santa Ynez Mountains for world-class trail hiking and mountain biking; zero local ski resorts (3+ hours to Mammoth).
profile.airport_distance: 10 miles (~15 min drive) to Santa Barbara Municipal Airport (SBA).
profile.transit_options: MTD local bus network serves campus heavily, though bikes and walking are the primary modes of transport for students.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: Laid-back beach town culture anchored directly by Isla Vista (IV)—a densely packed, legendary student enclave right outside the campus gates where streets are swarming with bikes, local surf shops, and casual food spots.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen are housed in diverse coastal residence halls like Manzanita and San Nicolas with immediate ocean views. Off-campus housing is hyper-concentrated in Isla Vista's high-density student apartments and multi-unit houses, where properties rent out nearly a year in advance and students typically share rooms or pack tightly into close quarters.
profile.medical_access: No on-campus teaching hospital, but connected via regional transit and close proximity to Cottage Health medical networks and local biotech research centers.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$43,937 (In-State CA). Final cost is largely fixed unless eligible for need-based aid.
details.Difficulty: Strict Pre-Bio GPA gatekeeping, brutal weed-out curves in Gen/Org Chem, and fast 10-week quarter pace.
details.Support: Fast quarter pace and overcrowded advising force high self-advocacy; help centers exist but are heavily TA-driven.
details.Adjustment: Identical coastal SoCal beach culture (Isla Vista), outdoorsy lifestyle, and easy drive/flight home.
details.Social: Legendary Isla Vista street and house party culture right on the ocean.
details.Environment: Unmatched daily access to coastal surfing, beach cruisers, and an active ocean lifestyle.
details.Weather: ~220 nice days. Mild coastal sun, minimal bad days
details.Biology: Top-tier R1 research; world-class molecular, cellular, and marine biology labs with strong West Coast biotech placement.
details.CLS: Pure theoretical bio; lacks clinical electives like Hematology and Quant Chem.
details.Spirit: No football team, but partially salvaged by a surprisingly massive, rowdy D1 men soccer culture that pulls thousands of students to Harder Stadium.
details.Happiness: 86 - High student satisfaction, beach setting, and strong campus community.
details.Admissions: Hard (F Grade): Selective UC system (~30% acceptance rate) heavily caps unweighted GPA and lacks test options, placing her UN GPA below the median admitted tier.

profile.topology: Picturesque rolling campus tucked right against the foothills of the Rocky Mountains with gentle slopes, beautiful stone pathways, and iconic outdoor gathering quads. Outdoors: Immediate walking access to the Flatirons for elite trail running and rock climbing; world-class skiing at Eldora (45 mins) and I-70 resorts (Vail/Copper within 1.5–2 hours); Boulder Creek path runs directly through campus.
profile.airport_distance: 28 miles (~40 min drive) to Denver International Airport (DEN) via regional highway and direct airport bus lines.
profile.transit_options: RTD regional bus system and the on-campus HOP transit route connect students seamlessly across Boulder and to local trailheads.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A classic picturesque mountain-town city feel. The campus flows right into 'The Hill' (a dense student commercial strip with pizza joints and cafes) and is a short walk from the upscale, brick-paved Pearl Street Mall. It feels distinctly upscale, active, and outdoors-obsessed.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features unique residential academic programs (RAPs) clustered around main campus. Off-campus housing in Boulder is notoriously expensive and fiercely competitive, requiring students to look months ahead for rentals in local complexes or shared suburban-style houses further from the central quad.
profile.medical_access: Campus medical services available via Wardenburg Health Center; proximal to Boulder Community Health facilities.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$64,452 - $68,440 (Out-of-State). Does not participate in WUE, but offers automatic non-resident merit scholarships based on GPA. Cost could lower slightly.
details.Difficulty: Rigorous Bio/Chem screening courses; strong R1 resources but requires heavy self-advocacy to get help.
details.Support: Good Science Learning Center tutoring and peer support hubs, though large lectures require self-driven outreach.
details.Adjustment: High sun and huge SoCal outdoor match (hiking/skiing); very smooth transition despite altitude.
details.Home: Easy: 5hr trip via 2.5hr flight + direct bus ($70-$130).
details.Social: Lively Pearl Street and The Hill, but less formal Greek dominance than the SEC.
details.Environment: World-class access for mountain biking, climbing the Flatirons, and weekend ski trips.
details.Weather: ~155 nice days. Cold snowy winters offset the crisp sunny days
details.Biology: BioFrontiers Institute powerhouse; deep federal funding and direct pipelines into the Boulder-Denver biotech/medical device hub.
details.CLS: Heavy research bio; missing clinical electives; requires external post-grad prereqs.
details.Spirit: Passionate Folsom Field crowd and prime Big 12 atmosphere, but sports dont totally rule campus life.
details.Happiness: 93 - Outstanding outdoor lifestyle, high student happiness, and campus amenities.
details.Admissions: Target (B Grade): Moderate competitiveness (~80% acceptance rate); values AP rigor and personal essays heavily; her 3.5-3.6 W GPA makes her a strong applicant for general/bio entry.

profile.topology: Flat, grid-based desert campus with iconic palm-lined pedestrian walkways (The Mall) that make walking and biking extremely easy across the entire layout. Outdoors: Surrounded by dramatic mountain ranges (Catalinas and Rincons) offering incredible desert hiking, rock climbing, and mountain biking within 20-30 minutes; landlocked with no major lakes or ocean; winter skiing available at Mount Lemmon (1 hour away).
profile.airport_distance: 9 miles (~20 min drive) to Tucson International Airport (TUS).
profile.transit_options: Sun Tran bus system and the modern Sun Link Streetcar running directly through campus and downtown Tucson.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: Urban-suburban desert setting. The campus blends directly into the vibrant Main Gate Square commercial district and is right next to the historic Fourth Avenue strip, offering local indie venues, casual taco shops, and a dense student-heavy off-campus grid.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen live in large-scale resort-style residence halls with heavy social integration. Off-campus housing is dominated by towering, high-rise luxury student apartment complexes clustered tightly around the edges of campus along Park Avenue and Speedway Boulevard, most within a 5-to-10 minute walk or scooter ride to class.
profile.medical_access: Full clinical access through Banner University Medical Center located adjacent to campus.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$65,900 - $67,770 (Out-of-State). Offers the Arizona Excellence Award ($6k-$18k/yr) for non-residents based on GPA. Cost could lower.
details.Difficulty: Massive intro lecture halls and self-driven environment; great research labs if you seek them out.
details.Support: Strong "Think Tank" tutoring network and Pre-Health advising, though massive intro halls require student initiative.
details.Adjustment: Desert sun, palm trees, and massive California student population; seamless cultural transition.
details.Social: Massive Greek life, pool parties, and a wild bar scene on Fourth Ave.
details.Environment: Great desert hiking and stargazing, but heavily landlocked and extremely hot.
details.Weather: ~175 nice days. Lovely winters but brutal Jun-Sep heat (110F+) penalized
details.Biology: BIO5 Institute heavy-hitter; exceptional interdisciplinary labs, pre-health tracks, and growing AZ bioscience ties.
details.CLS: Strong Physiology/Med Bio tracks; covers core chem/micro, but no direct main-campus MLS BS.
details.Spirit: Rivalry-fueled Wildcat sports culture; massive basketball tradition and rowdy football tailgates.
details.Happiness: 85 - Great weather, active campus social life, and high student satisfaction.
details.Admissions: Easy (A Grade): Accessible admissions (~86% acceptance rate); grid/index-based admissions heavily driven by core GPA requirements, making entry practically assured.

profile.topology: Flat urban-suburban campus layout featuring broad pedestrian malls, open green spaces, and integrated light rail access across the Tempe metro. Outdoors: Right next to Tempe Town Lake for kayaking and paddleboarding; local hiking at 'A' Mountain (Papago Park) on campus borders; major mountain trails (Camelback/Superstitions) within 20-30 minutes; no nearby ocean or skiing (3+ hours to Flagstaff).
profile.airport_distance: 7 miles (~10-15 min drive) to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX).
profile.transit_options: Valley Metro Light Rail station directly on campus alongside extensive local bus routes and free neighborhood circulators.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A bustling urban city environment centered right next to downtown Tempe. Mill Avenue runs parallel to campus with high-rise bars, shopping, and restaurants, creating an energetic city vibe that seamlessly merges with the massive student population.
profile.housing_status: Modern residential 'villages' cluster freshmen tightly by major. Off-campus housing consists of sprawling high-rise apartment towers lining University Drive and Apache Boulevard, many featuring resort-style pools and private shuttle options to combat the desert heat.
profile.medical_access: Integrated health services on-campus and close proximity to Valley-wide clinical networks.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$55,091 - $57,000 (Out-of-State). Tempe main campus does NOT offer WUE, but provides generous New American University merit scholarships based on GPA.
details.Difficulty: Early-warning tracking tech, 24/7 tutoring, and structured SI sessions keep large STEM classes manageable.
details.Support: Industry-leading eAdvising tech with automated early-warning flags, 24/7 tutoring, and proactive SI study sessions.
details.Adjustment: Sunny year-round, giant SoCal transplant crowd, and familiar desert/coastal lifestyle blend.
details.Home: Easy: 5.5hr drive (~$55 gas) or 3.5hr trip via 1.25hr flight ($40-$80).
details.Social: The ultimate nightlife scale: Mill Ave, massive concerts, and huge Greek presence.
details.Environment: Highly urbanized; great city amenities but requires driving out of the metro for real nature escapes.
details.Weather: ~150 nice days. Phoenix heat island makes bad days worse than Tucson
details.Biology: Biodesign Institute engine; cutting-edge facilities and strong health-tech pipelines in the Phoenix metro.
details.CLS: Offers a direct Medical Laboratory Science (BAS) degree with NAACLS-aligned clinical coursework.
details.Spirit: Massive Sun Devil athletics presence; loud Big 12 game days and major campus-wide spirit.
details.Happiness: 85 - High campus energy, modern facilities, and top-tier student recreation.
details.Admissions: Easy (A Grade): Highly accessible (~90% acceptance rate); strict assured-admissions criteria based on GPA/test scores where her 3.5+ W GPA guarantees entry.

profile.topology: Flat, historic, and beautifully shaded campus centered around 'The Oval,' with dedicated bike lanes and extremely easy pedestrian navigation. Outdoors: Immediate access to Horsetooth Reservoir for boating/paddleboarding; world-class mountain biking and hiking trails directly bordering the foothills; skiing in the Rockies (Estes Park/Loveland) within 1 to 1.5 hours.
profile.airport_distance: 65 miles (~1 hr 15 min drive) north to Denver International Airport (DEN), with convenient Bustang shuttle options.
profile.transit_options: MAX Bus Rapid Transit system running directly through campus, connecting Fort Collins from north to south.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A classic, thriving Colorado mountain town. The campus sits a short, scenic bike ride away from historic 'Old Town' Fort Collins, which features Victorian-style brick storefronts, local craft breweries, and an extremely friendly, outdoors-oriented community feel.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features robust residential learning communities on campus. Off-campus options consist largely of multi-family rental houses and mid-rise complexes stretching toward Old Town, where biking or taking the MAX bus makes commuting seamless.
profile.medical_access: Clinical partnerships with UCHealth Medical Center of the Rockies and local regional clinics.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$50,000 - $53,294 (Out-of-State). Participates in WUE (3.2+ GPA required). High likelihood of cost lowering.
details.Difficulty: Premier vet/life-science teaching focus; peer mentoring and collaborative labs minimize weed-out stress.
details.Support: Dedicated STEM peer-mentoring, highly accessible faculty, and learning communities built around undergrad retention.
details.Adjustment: Great laid-back outdoor culture; feels slightly more local/traditional Colorado than Boulder.
details.Social: Laid-back brewery and live music town; missing the massive blowout party reputation.
details.Environment: Immediate access to Horsetooth Reservoir, Rocky Mountain trails, and outdoor recreation.
details.Weather: ~155 nice days. Cold winters and high plains wind offset the sun
details.Biology: Legendary vet-med, microbiology, and animal science programs; exceptional hands-on labs across the Front Range.
details.CLS: Microbiology BS has strong clinical tracks and a direct feeder partnership with CCMLS.
details.Spirit: Loud Ram pride with a modern on-campus stadium, but regional and lacks the massive, all-consuming SEC game-day culture.
details.Happiness: 89 - Excellent college town environment, high student well-being, and outdoor access.
details.Admissions: Easy (A Grade): Highly accessible (~90% acceptance rate); admissions criteria readily admit students clearing a 3.0+ GPA threshold.

profile.topology: Compact, historic urban-campus layout featuring brick pathways, shaded quads (The Horseshoe), and relatively flat walking terrain. Outdoors: Access to the Congaree River and Lake Murray for kayaking and boating; flat local wooded trails, but no significant mountains or skiing within a reasonable day trip; coastal beaches are roughly 2 hours away.
profile.airport_distance: 7 miles (~15 min drive) to Columbia Metropolitan Airport (CAE).
profile.transit_options: COMET bus system and student-operated shuttles offering reliable connectivity across campus and downtown Columbia.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A classic Southern state-capital city setting. The campus weaves directly into downtown Columbia and is right next to the historic 'Five Points' district—a lively neighborhood strip filled with local bars, eateries, and Southern storefronts.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features historic halls around The Horseshoe as well as massive modern residential complexes like Green Quad. Off-campus housing is heavily influenced by Greek village houses and managed student apartments spread across downtown and the Vista district.
profile.medical_access: Integrated student health and access to Prisma Health hospital systems.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$55,800 (Out-of-State). Offers aggressive non-resident merit scholarships for high GPAs that can lower out-of-state tuition close to in-state rates.
details.Difficulty: Nationally top-ranked advising network with structured Supplemental Instruction (SI) in tough sciences.
details.Support: Nationally top-ranked Student Success Center with extensive Supplemental Instruction (SI) and hands-on academic coaching.
details.Adjustment: Significant shift to SEC Greek life, traditional Southern pacing, and a completely different social ecosystem.
details.Home: Hard: 8+hr trip via multi-leg flights; expensive ($275-$475+).
details.Social: Elite SEC Greek life and chaotic Five Points bar scene right off campus.
details.Environment: Landlocked with heavy humidity; outdoor recreation is highly limited compared to the West Coast.
details.Weather: ~130 nice days. Humid muggy summers drag the score down hard
details.Biology: Solid pre-med tracks and regional hospital networks, but lacks a dense local corporate biotech corridor.
details.CLS: Solid pre-med/bio curriculum; easily covers core prereqs with in-state clinical pipelines.
details.Spirit: Elite SEC football religion; iconic Five Points tailgating and intense, stadium-shaking spirit.
details.Happiness: 88 - Deep SEC campus pride, active student body, and vibrant campus life.
details.Admissions: Hard (D Grade): Competitive review (~57% acceptance rate); holistic review process that rewards her AP coursework and strong essay writing.

profile.topology: Flat, historic Pacific Northwest campus featuring towering old-growth trees, brick architecture, and extensive dedicated bike paths. Outdoors: Instant access to the Willamette River and McDonald-Dunn Forest for trail running and mountain biking; Cascade Mountains and skiing (Hoodoo/Willamette Pass) within 1 to 1.5 hours; Pacific Ocean beaches are roughly 1 hour west.
profile.airport_distance: 45 miles (~50 min drive) north to Eugene Airport (EUG) or 90 miles to Portland International (PDX).
profile.transit_options: Corvallis Transit System (CTS) provides fareless local bus service across the entire city and campus footprint.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A quintessential, peaceful Pacific Northwest college town. Downtown Corvallis sits right next to the Willamette River with indie coffee shops and local bookstores, creating an unhurried, bike-centric, and intensely green community feel.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features diverse residence halls across campus. Off-campus housing consists primarily of affordable local apartment complexes and cozy rental houses scattered through quiet neighborhoods where biking is the default transit method.
profile.medical_access: Access via Good Samaritan Regional Medical Center and university-affiliated health clinics.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$58,668 (Out-of-State). Participates in WUE based on high school GPA. High likelihood of cost lowering.
details.Difficulty: Dedicated Science Success Center tutoring and early paid research access (URSA-Engage) drive high retention.
details.Support: Science Success Center offers dedicated STEM tutoring and early paid research mentorship (URSA-Engage).
details.Adjustment: West Coast outdoorsy vibe; heavily aligned with SoCal lifestyle values despite the regional shift.
details.Home: Hard: 6.5hr trip via 2.5hr flight + long shuttle ($170-$210).
details.Social: Quiet, subdued campus nightlife; mostly smaller house parties and local pubs.
details.Environment: Great access to the Cascades and coast, but persistent rain limits daily outdoor consistency.
details.Weather: ~105 nice days. Relentless PNW grey and rain
details.Biology: Elite ag/forestry research with massive federal grants; top-tier environmental biology and biochemistry labs.
details.CLS: Features a dedicated BioHealth Sciences major with an official Pre-Clinical Lab Science option.
details.Spirit: Loyal Reser Stadium culture and proud Beaver backing, but quiet nationally and overshadowed by larger regional powerhouses.
details.Happiness: 82 - High marks for campus safety, friendly community, and outdoor culture.
details.Admissions: Target (B Grade): Accessible admissions (~78% acceptance rate); holistic but accessible admissions where her 3.5+ W GPA and AP background put her in a great spot.

profile.topology: Built on a mesa with distinct slopes and stairways connecting upper and lower campus, but compact enough to cross on foot in 20 minutes. Outdoors: 15-20 minutes to Mission Trails Regional Park for hiking and mountain biking; Pacific Ocean beaches (Mission/Pacific Beach) are 20 minutes west for surfing and coastal runs; zero local ski resorts (hours away).
profile.airport_distance: 12 miles (~15-20 min drive) to San Diego International Airport (SAN).
profile.transit_options: Direct MTS Green Line Trolley station on campus connecting straight to downtown and Mission Valley.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A dense, student-centric urban-suburban neighborhood setting (College Area). The immediate blocks surrounding campus are packed with student-frequented burger joints, boba shops, and apartment complexes, with fast trolley access into North Park and downtown.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen are clustered in modern residence halls near Cuicacallia Suites and the central quad. Off-campus housing is intensely competitive, with students renting houses or apartments in the immediate surrounding neighborhoods (often referred to as 'The College Area') or commuting from nearby coastal suburbs.
profile.medical_access: No primary on-campus teaching hospital, but positioned within 30 minutes of major research and medical powerhouses like UCSD Health and the Torrey Pines Mesa biotech cluster.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$37,324 - $38,938 (In-State CA). Final cost is largely fixed unless eligible for local/need-based aid.
details.Difficulty: Impacted biology major; large intro lectures and high demand require proactive office hour visits.
details.Support: Impacted biology major causes advising slots to fill fast; resources exist but the system wont hunt you down.
details.Adjustment: Zero adjustment; home turf in San Diego with familiar local network, weather, and coastal lifestyle.
details.Social: Massive Southern California party reputation and huge local nightlife access.
details.Environment: Perfect year-round weather for coastal surfing, hiking, and active local sports leagues.
details.Weather: ~250 nice days. Peak SoCal perfection, minimal bad days
details.Biology: Leverages San Diego’s top-3 global biotech hub (Torrey Pines Mesa) for unmatched local interning and lab access.
details.CLS: Microbiology BS offers an explicit Clinical Lab Science emphasis including Hematology.
details.Spirit: Good basketball energy and new Snapdragon Stadium tailgating, but heavily diluted by the broader San Diego lifestyle.
details.Happiness: 84 - Strong local lifestyle, high campus satisfaction, and great climate.
details.Admissions: Hard (F Grade): Highly impacted (~36% acceptance rate); CSUs use a strict numerical algorithm weighted on raw GPA without essays; impacted Bio major keeps entry tight.

profile.topology: Hillside campus nestled against the Wasatch Range, featuring sloping terrain, scenic elevated views of Salt Lake City, and modern architectural clusters. Outdoors: Immediate access to world-class mountain biking and hiking trails right up Red Butte and Emigration Canyons; elite skiing at Alta/Snowbird and Park City within 30-45 minutes; Great Salt Lake is nearby.
profile.airport_distance: 10 miles (~20 min drive) to Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC).
profile.transit_options: UTA TRAX light rail red line and campus shuttle network offering free transit for students across the Salt Lake valley.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: An urban-mountain fusion setting right at the edge of downtown Salt Lake City. The campus sits elevated against the Wasatch foothills, giving it a peaceful, nature-forward academic enclave feel while remaining a short TRAX ride away from the city's urban grid.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features extensive modern complexes built originally for the Olympic Village. Off-campus housing is widely spread throughout the surrounding Salt Lake neighborhoods (like the Avenues or Sugar House), though many students rely on the free TRAX system to commute if they live off-site.
profile.medical_access: University of Utah Health provides a premier on-campus teaching hospital and clinical research system.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$45,415 - $51,135 (Out-of-State). Eligible for WUE with a 3.30+ GPA, capping tuition at 150% of in-state. High likelihood of cost lowering.
details.Difficulty: Direct med center access with funded undergrad research (UROP) and collaborative STEM support.
details.Support: Well-funded STEM tutoring hubs and direct Health Sciences advising with accessible undergrad research mentors.
details.Adjustment: Progressive college pockets, but embedded in a distinct regional and religious cultural backdrop.
details.Home: Moderate: 4hr trip via 2hr flight; tickets pricey ($200-$300).
details.Social: Very muted nightlife due to local liquor laws and a heavy commuter population.
details.Environment: Unbeatable access to world-class ski canyons within 30 minutes of campus.
details.Weather: ~150 nice days. Cold winters plus inversions hurt air quality badly
details.Biology: World-renowned genetics and biochemistry labs with direct ties to U of U Health and Intermountain West biotech.
details.CLS: Features a direct, NAACLS-accredited BS in Medical Laboratory Science with clinical rotations.
details.Spirit: Passionate Utes fanbase and elite football atmosphere in Rice-Eccles, though slightly more regional compared to elite SEC flagships.
details.Happiness: 87 - Excellent campus facilities, mountain backdrop, and high overall student life.
details.Admissions: Target (B Grade): Accessible admissions (~87% acceptance rate); high acceptance rate with broad admissions criteria where her GPA profile is well above average.

profile.topology: Rolling, picturesque Southern campus featuring historic brick buildings, beautiful oak-lined quads, and gently sloping terrain. Outdoors: Access to local Chewacla State Park for mountain biking and lake swimming; Lake Martin is 30 minutes away for boating; no local mountains, skiing, or ocean access.
profile.airport_distance: 55 miles (~50 min drive) west to Montgomery Regional Airport (MGM) or 100 miles to Atlanta (ATL).
profile.transit_options: Tiger Transit bus system providing extensive complimentary transportation across campus and the local Auburn area.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A quintessential, tight-knit Southern SEC college town. Downtown Auburn merges right into the campus edge at the iconic Toomer's Corner, characterized by local Southern dining, historic storefronts, and an overwhelmingly warm, small-town community atmosphere.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features high-end residence halls managed through the 'Auburn Family' residential program. Off-campus housing consists of sprawling student complexes and cottage communities built specifically for upperclassmen, many featuring massive pools and private shuttle loops.
profile.medical_access: University-affiliated medical support services and proximal to regional care providers.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$56,706 - $58,000 (Out-of-State). Offers structured non-resident merit scholarships based on GPA and test scores. Cost could lower.
details.Difficulty: Dedicated COSAm STEM tutoring centers, strong pre-health advising, and accessible faculty mentorship.
details.Support: COSAM features structured drop-in STEM tutoring centers, dedicated pre-health advisors, and close faculty ties.
details.Adjustment: Significant shift to SEC Greek life, traditional Southern pacing, and a completely different social ecosystem.
details.Home: Hard: 7.5hr trip via flight + shuttle; expensive ($200-$400+).
details.Social: Legendary SEC tailgating and massive traditional Greek life dominance.
details.Environment: Lake Martin is great, but day-to-day dynamic outdoor terrain is very limited.
details.Weather: ~125 nice days. Deep South heat and humidity punish the bad days
details.Biology: Strong pre-vet and agricultural tracks, but traditional corporate biotech/industrial bio networking lags behind.
details.CLS: Main campus covers core prereqs in Biomedical Sci; full NAACLS MLS is at Auburn Montgomery.
details.Spirit: Peak SEC tradition; Toomers Corner, legendary tailgating, and total town-wide football immersion.
details.Happiness: 98 - Near-top national satisfaction rating; legendary campus spirit, food, and student community.
details.Admissions: Hard (D Grade): Competitive out-of-state pool (~50% acceptance rate); admissions leans heavily on GPA metrics and academic alignment.

profile.topology: Flat, highly walkable, and tree-lined campus with historic brick quadrangles and modern sustainability-focused facilities. Outdoors: Bordered by the Willamette River and Skinner Butte for quick trail runs; Cascade Mountains and winter skiing (Hoodoo/Willamette Pass) within 1 to 1.5 hours; Pacific Coast beaches are roughly 1 hour west.
profile.airport_distance: 10 miles (~15 min drive) to Eugene Airport (EUG).
profile.transit_options: Lane Transit District (LTD) bus network offering free rides for UO students across the Eugene-Springfield area.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A progressive Pacific Northwest city-town hybrid. The campus borders the lively West University neighborhood, which is packed with local food trucks, coffee houses, and indie vintage stores, carrying a distinctively artsy, green, and bike-heavy culture.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen live in modern residence halls close to the Erb Memorial Union. Off-campus housing consists heavily of shared student rentals and mid-rise apartment buildings throughout the West University district within easy walking or biking distance.
profile.medical_access: Integrated student health and proximity to Eugene-area medical and trauma centers.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$68,931 - $74,325 (Out-of-State). Does not participate in WUE, but offers automatic Apex/Summit merit scholarships based on GPA. Cost could lower.
details.Difficulty: Smaller STEM class sizes than massive land-grants and good tutoring, but moderate local clinical access.
details.Support: Solid support via the Tutoring & Academic Engagement Center; smaller STEM scale allows better advisor access.
details.Adjustment: West Coast outdoorsy vibe; heavily aligned with SoCal lifestyle values despite the regional shift.
details.Social: Strong house party and bar scene, but lacks the sheer massive scale of ASU or LSU.
details.Environment: Deep PNW recreation in the Cascades, though winter rain dampens daily outdoor activities.
details.Weather: ~105 nice days. Wet PNW marine climate, relentlessly grey
details.Biology: Respectable molecular biology and neuroscience (Institute of Molecular Biology), but smaller overall scope than peers.
details.CLS: Solid West Coast bio/micro curriculum; covers general prereqs, though lacks on-campus MLS.
details.Spirit: Iconic Autzen Stadium noise, Nike-backed hype, and massive statewide Duck pride.
details.Happiness: 79 - Solid Pacific Northwest campus life, though dinged slightly on housing and weather.
details.Admissions: Target (B Grade): Moderate selectiveness (~78% acceptance rate); holistic review that places solid value on AP course load and personal statement essays.

profile.topology: Expansive, flat Southern campus featuring magnificent live oak trees, Italian Renaissance-style architecture, and picturesque lakes. Outdoors: Situated right along the Mississippi River with campus lakes for walking; virtually zero dynamic elevation, mountains, or skiing; Gulf Coast beaches are 2+ hours south.
profile.airport_distance: 9 miles (~15 min drive) to Baton Rouge Metropolitan Airport (BTR) or 75 miles to New Orleans (MSY).
profile.transit_options: Tiger Trails campus bus service connecting students across all residential and academic zones.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A sprawling Southern capital city setting. The campus is self-contained along the Mississippi River, bordered by suburban residential extensions and bustling commercial corridors characterized by heavy local Southern culture and legendary game-day energy.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features historic and modern residential colleges across campus. Off-campus housing is dominated by sprawling luxury apartment complexes and rental properties off Highland Road and Burbank Drive, which require driving or shuttle utilization to reach central classes.
profile.medical_access: Access to comprehensive university medical clinics and proximity to Baton Rouge General health systems.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$56,122 - $58,256 (Out-of-State). Offers automatic non-resident merit scholarships and fee waivers for high GPAs and test scores. Cost could lower.
details.Difficulty: High DFW (Drop/Fail/Withdraw) rates in General & Organic Chem with traditional sink-or-swim dynamics.
details.Support: Center for Academic Success provides solid SI study sessions, though main academic advising is more reactive.
details.Adjustment: Largest cultural shift on the list: heavy Cajun/subtropical environment, unique local customs, and deep-rooted SEC identity.
details.Home: Hard: 9hr trip via multi-leg flights; very expensive ($325-$525+).
details.Social: Tigerland and SEC tailgating create one of the most intense party environments in the country.
details.Environment: Flat, swampy, and intensely humid; virtually zero traditional dynamic outdoor recreation.
details.Weather: ~95 nice days. Subtropical humidity makes bad days genuinely oppressive
details.Biology: Solid regional bio departments and local medical ties, but institutional biotech research funding is relatively limited.
details.CLS: Has an established Medical Laboratory Science pipeline linked directly to LSU Health Sciences.
details.Spirit: Unrivaled Death Valley night games, legendary Cajun tailgating, and pure football-as-religion culture.
details.Happiness: 81 - Intense game day passion, though campus infrastructure and housing hold score down.
details.Admissions: Target (C Grade): Straightforward benchmarks (~79% acceptance rate); weighted GPA comfortably exceeds requirements.

profile.topology: Flat, tropical South Florida campus layout featuring modern architecture, sunny outdoor courtyards, and close proximity to coastal waterways. Outdoors: Minutes from Atlantic Ocean beaches for swimming, surfing, and paddleboarding; flat local coastal paths, but zero mountains or skiing anywhere in Florida (completely flat terrain).
profile.airport_distance: 26 miles (~30 min drive) to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL) or Palm Beach International (PBI).
profile.transit_options: Boca Raton Tri-Rail shuttle service connecting students directly to regional transit systems and local commercial centers.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: An upscale, quiet suburban South Florida setting. The campus sits in wealthy Boca Raton just minutes from pristine Atlantic beaches and high-end outdoor malls, carrying a relaxed, palm-lined coastal vibe rather than a dense, walkable college town feel.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen live in modern resort-style residence halls like Innovation Village Apartments. Off-campus housing is expensive and upscale, dominated by suburban rental units and luxury apartment complexes across Boca Raton where most students require a car to get around.
profile.medical_access: Access to local university health services and proximal to regional Baptist Health networks.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$42,382 - $46,422 (Out-of-State). Offers non-resident merit scholarships based on GPA. Cost could lower after admission.
details.Difficulty: Dedicated B.S. in Medical Bio track with Peer-Led Team Learning (PLTL) support in tough O-Chem sequences.
details.Support: Strong Center for Learning and Student Success (CLASS) utilizing Peer-Led Team Learning (PLTL) in tough STEM series.
details.Adjustment: Familiar sunny coastal/beach lifestyle, but a distinct East Coast/suburban adjustment away from the West Coast vibe.
details.Social: Sleepy campus in a wealthy suburb; requires a drive to Miami/Fort Lauderdale for real nightlife.
details.Environment: Close to South Florida beaches, but embedded in flat, humid urban sprawl.
details.Weather: ~175 nice days. Beautiful winters but summer humidity and hurricane risk penalized
details.Biology: Decent regional Florida pre-health tracks, but lacks a heavy research corridor or major biotech pipeline.
details.CLS: Solid Medical Biology tracks; good access to regional Florida hospital MLS internship sites.
details.Spirit: Subdued athletic culture; smaller commuter crowds and minimal traditional game-day energy.
details.Happiness: 66 - Lower student satisfaction; heavy commuter feel and limited residential campus life.
details.Admissions: Target (C Grade): Accessible core GPA requirements (~60% acceptance rate) where her academic profile sits well within standard entry bands.
